The Summoner, designated Thor by Inner Sphere forces, is a 70-ton Clan OmniMech introduced in 2872 by Clan Jade Falcon. The design emerged shortly after the Jade Falcons became the first Clan to win OmniMech technology from Clan Coyote in 2863, making the Summoner one of the earliest second-generation OmniMechs ever produced. Jade Falcon engineers combined technology derived from the Coyote Warlock OmniMech with captured Thresher BattleMech chassis to create a versatile heavy platform capable of filling multiple battlefield roles.

Produced primarily by the Eagle Craft Group and other Clan manufacturers, the Summoner became a signature design of the Jade Falcon touman and one of the most widely recognized Clan OmniMechs in the Inner Sphere. Its combination of speed, firepower, and jump capability has kept it in continuous production for nearly three centuries, earning it the distinction of being one of the longest-serving OmniMechs in existence.

The Summoner achieves its remarkable versatility through a balanced combination of speed, firepower, and protection. Powered by a Redline 350 XL engine, the seventy-ton chassis reaches speeds of just over eighty-six kilometers per hour, while five permanently mounted JF Standard jump jets provide a jump capability of one hundred and fifty meters. This combination of ground speed and jump capability gives the Summoner mobility that rivals many medium OmniMechs, allowing it to dictate engagement ranges and exploit terrain to an unusual degree for a heavy design.

Nine and a half tons of J63-3E Ferro Fibrous armor provide respectable protection for the chassis weight, though the design sacrifices maximum armor coverage to preserve its generous twenty-two and a half tons of pod space. In its Primary configuration, the Summoner carries an ER PPC in the right arm for devastating long-range strikes, an LB 10-X Autocannon in the left arm for flexible direct fire, and an LRM-15 in the left torso for indirect fire support. This combination of energy, ballistic, and missile weaponry allows a single Summoner to engage effectively across all range brackets.

The fixed jump jets represent both a strength and a design constraint. While they ensure every configuration benefits from superior tactical mobility, they consume tonnage and critical space that cannot be reallocated, limiting the pod space available compared to competing heavy OmniMechs that mount jump jets as pod equipment. This trade-off has proven acceptable in practice, as the Summoner's consistent mobility across all configurations remains one of its defining tactical advantages.

The Summoner's history is inextricably linked to the rise of Clan Jade Falcon as a military power. When the Jade Falcons won OmniMech technology from Clan Coyote in 2863, they moved quickly to develop their own designs. The Summoner was among the first results, entering production at Eagle Craft Group facilities on Ironhold and rapidly becoming the backbone of Falcon heavy OmniMech forces. St. Louis MechWorks on Niles, operating under Clan Hell's Horses control, established a parallel production line that ensured the design's availability beyond Falcon territory. Kindraa Kline of Clan Fire Mandrill also maintained limited production at their facility on Dagda, though in far smaller numbers.

During Operation REVIVAL, the Summoner was three times as common in Jade Falcon units as in any other Clan's forces, and it was during this campaign that Victor Steiner-Davion assigned the reporting name Thor after his personal encounter with the design on Trellwan. The name proved fitting, the combination of a PPC's lightning and an autocannon's thunder made an indelible impression on Inner Sphere commanders. A Clan Coyote adage born of the Invasion warned that encountering a Falcon outside a Summoner, Hellbringer, or Kit Fox warranted doubling one's caution, proof of how thoroughly the design defined Jade Falcon tactical doctrine.

The Wars of Reaving reshaped the Summoner's production theater dramatically. The Ghost Bear facility on Bearclaw, which had produced Summoners since the design's early years, passed to Clan Snow Raven and later to Clan Stone Lion as alliances and absorptions shifted Clan territories. The Fire Mandrill facility on Dagda fell under Clan Goliath Scorpion and then Clan Star Adder control. Meanwhile, the Jade Falcon factory on Vantaa was destroyed when the planet was rendered uninhabitable during fighting between the Hell's Horses and Ice Hellions in 3072.

In the Inner Sphere occupation zones, the Jade Falcons expanded Summoner production through Eagle Craft Group operations on Erewhon and mobile factory assets, while Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten briefly hosted a production line during the Jihad era. The Hell's Horses, having long maintained production on Niles through St. Louis MechWorks, added a new line at Svarstaad Industriplex Gamma after capturing that world. This proved prescient, as the Jade Falcons increasingly shifted their heavy OmniMech production to the Grand Summoner during the Dark Age, leaving the Hell's Horses as the primary champions of the original design.

By 3150, the Summoner had served continuously for nearly three centuries, an almost unmatched record for any OmniMech. Clan Hell's Horses embraced the design for both training and front-line service, introducing new configurations that incorporated modern weapons technology while retaining the chassis's proven mobility and reliability. The Hell's Horses' continued investment ensured that the Summoner remained a relevant battlefield presence well into the ilClan era, even as newer designs increasingly dominated the rosters of other Clans.

The Sunder is a ninety-ton Inner Sphere OmniMech developed by the Draconis Combine as the assault class component of the DCMS first generation of domestically produced OmniMechs. Introduced in 3056, the design was born from the intensive study of captured Clan Hellbringer and Summoner chassis following the Battle of Luthien in 3052. Draconis Combine engineers at Luthien Armor Works determined the leg assemblies of both progenitor designs could support twenty additional tons of mass, though overcoming catastrophic actuator burnout in prototypes and resolving caustic exhaust fouling from torso-mounted pod bays delayed the Sunder's entry into service, making it among the last of the first-generation DCMS OmniMechs to reach full production.

Though initially a Combine-exclusive design, the Sunder's proven chassis attracted interest from multiple successor states, and licensed production eventually spread the assault OmniMech to militaries across the Inner Sphere. This broad manufacturing base has kept the Sunder in continuous service from the Clan Invasion era through the ilClan period.

The Sunder is built around a Hermes 360 XL engine that propels the ninety-ton chassis to a top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour. The bulky engine forced designers to relocate the torso OmniPod bays above the cockpit, an arrangement that contributed to early exhaust fouling problems but provides thirty-six tons of available pod space. Sixteen and a half tons of Mitchell Argon armor give the Sunder respectable protection for an assault 'Mech, while fifteen fixed double heat sinks manage the thermal load across most configurations.

In its Prime configuration, the Sunder is built for devastating close-range engagements. An Autocannon/20 forms the core of its firepower, supported by two large lasers for medium-range engagement, a trio of SRM-4 launchers, and two medium lasers. This loadout makes the Prime variant most lethal at short ranges, though the large lasers provide adequate reach to engage enemies closing on its position.

While thirty-six tons of pod space theoretically make the Sunder a powerful combatant, its reduced ground speed and reliance on less efficient Inner Sphere weaponry leave it at a disadvantage compared to many Clan assault OmniMechs. The widespread use of salvaged Clan OmniPods during Operation Bulldog finally allowed the Sunder to compete on more equal footing with designs such as the Warhawk and Executioner.

The Sunder's origins lie in the aftermath of the Battle of Luthien in 3052, when Draconis Combine forces captured examples of the Clan Hellbringer and Summoner OmniMechs. Combine engineers at Luthien Armor Works began an ambitious program to reverse-engineer these designs for domestic manufacture, selecting the assault weight class as one of several parallel development efforts alongside the Avatar and other first-generation OmniMechs. Prototype Sunders suffered from catastrophic actuator failure as the heavier chassis overstressed components designed for lighter Clan machines, and additional problems with caustic exhaust residue from torso-mounted weapons fouling the cockpit canopy and sensor arrays required extensive rework before full production could begin in 3056.

Initial deployment saw Sunders assigned to assault lances stationed along the Clan border, where they played a significant role during Operation Bulldog. The DCMS authorization for widespread use of salvaged Clan weaponry in OmniPods proved transformative, as Sunders equipped with Clan-grade weapons could finally compete favorably against Clan Warhawk and Executioner OmniMechs. Many Sunders also served as the anchor point of DCMS command networks, with dedicated C3 configurations enabling lance and company-level coordination that proved its effectiveness during the conflict.

StarCorps Industries recognized the Sunder's potential and licensed production from Luthien Armor Works in the early 3060s, establishing manufacturing lines at their plants on Crofton, Loburg, Son Hoa, and St. Ives. This licensing arrangement proved fortuitous when the Word of Blake Jihad devastated the DCMS's industrial base. Luthien Armor Works' OmniMech production facility was destroyed during the opening stages of the Jihad, cutting off the Combine's primary source of Sunders. StarCorps continued production for the Federated Suns, Lyran Alliance, and Capellan Confederation, ensuring the design survived even as the DCMS lost access to new production.

The Sunder continued to see combat during the tensions surrounding the Lyons Thumb and throughout the First Combine-Dominion War, where its role as a C3 network anchor proved particularly valuable. In the Dark Age era, new configurations incorporating Clan-spec weaponry and advanced electronics such as C3 boosted slave units and TSEMP cannons demonstrated the chassis's continued relevance. StarCorps facilities on Crofton and Loburg maintained production into the ilClan era, keeping the Sunder in service across multiple successor states long after its original Combine-only production had ended.

The Tempest is a sixty-five-ton heavy BattleMech designed by Irian BattleMechs Unlimited as a replacement for the aging Thunderbolt in Free Worlds League service. Originating in the late 3040s and relying on little advanced technology, the Clan Invasion and resulting research and development effort led to radical modifications, and the production model fielded in 3055 bore little resemblance to the initial concept. Irian BattleMechs Unlimited produces the Tempest at facilities on both Irian and Angell II, and the design has earned a reputation as a versatile and well-balanced heavy combatant that has proven difficult to improve upon. Combat operations have prompted the creation of several variants as both field modifications and factory-built options.

The Tempest's primary armament centers on a Zeus Slingshot Gauss rifle, delivering devastating long-range firepower without generating waste heat. A Sutel Precision Line large pulse laser supplements this at medium to long ranges, while three Diplan M3 medium lasers and an Irian Weapons Works 60mm SRM-6 rack provide punishing close-range firepower. The Gauss rifle carries two tons of ammunition for sixteen rounds of fire, and the SRM-6 has one ton of ammunition providing fifteen salvos.

The original design concept called for twin PPCs, but Irian designers replaced this configuration with the Gauss rifle and large pulse laser combination for the production model. Four Chilton 465 jump jets grant the Tempest a one hundred twenty meter jump capability, allowing it to keep pace with many lighter 'Mechs despite a mediocre cruising speed of forty-three kilometers per hour. Fine-tuning and testing on Irian's varied landscapes led the manufacturer to claim the Tempest operates across any terrain without loss of capability, an assertion the League military has tested on several occasions. Twelve tons of Maximillian 100 armor provide respectable protection for a sixty-five ton chassis, though the lack of CASE leaves the XL engine vulnerable to catastrophic ammunition explosions.

The Tempest's origins trace to the late 3040s, when Irian BattleMechs Unlimited began developing a replacement for the venerable Thunderbolt in Free Worlds League service. The project initially used little advanced technology, but the shock of the Clan Invasion in 3049 prompted massive investment in research and development across the Inner Sphere. The Tempest design was radically overhauled to incorporate newly recovered Star League-era technologies, and the production TMP-3M that rolled off the Irian assembly line in 3055 was fundamentally different from the original prototype.

The Tempest's introduction immediately created friction within the Free Worlds League's defense industry. When Earthwerks attempted to market their updated TDR-9M Thunderbolt variant, Irian BattleMechs Unlimited lobbied the League Central Coordination and Command to halt new Thunderbolt production, arguing the Tempest rendered further Thunderbolt development unnecessary. The resulting corporate dispute was only resolved when the Word of Blake brokered a compromise, pitting the two designs against each other in a combat trial to determine which would supply the Blakist military.

Free Worlds military strategists embraced the Tempest, deploying it throughout the FWLM in formations that deliberately echoed Star League Defense Force doctrine. Lance- and company-sized Tempest units, often paired with the lighter Shadow Hawk, created flexible strike forces capable of rapid offensive and defensive operations. The largest concentrations served in the Marik Militias, Free Worlds Legions, and Fusiliers of Oriente. The design made its greatest impression in the Sirian Lancers, where its balance of firepower and agility proved vital during Operation Guerrero and the subsequent liberation of Sirius and Procyon.

The Jihad devastated the Tempest's production infrastructure. The Irian facility fell under Word of Blake control, and while production continued under Blakist oversight, many Free Worlds League units found themselves cut off from spare parts and replacement chassis. The establishment of the Angell II production line by Irian Technologies helped offset this loss, though the facility did not reach operational capacity until 3077. Following the Jihad, the Republic of the Sphere assumed control of both facilities, allegedly taking the Irian line offline during the 3090s, though production reportedly continued in secret.

The collapse of the Republic and the reformation of the Free Worlds League saw Irian BattleMechs Unlimited regain control of its production lines. Regarded as a difficult design to improve upon, it took until the 3130s for a formal successor variant to debut. New variants including the TMP-4M and the Clan Protectorate-backed Tempest C emerged during the Dark Age, demonstrating the design's continued relevance more than eight decades after its introduction.

The Templar III is a Dark Age era eighty-five ton assault OmniMech produced by General Motors for the Federated Suns. Introduced around 3100, it was designed as a direct replacement for the original Templar after the destruction of Kallon Industries' factory on Talon during the Jihad eliminated production of the first-generation design. General Motors established a new production line on New Valencia to continue the Templar legacy with updated technologies.

Like its predecessor, the Templar III serves primarily as a command 'Mech for AFFS assault formations. The design incorporates advanced equipment across its alternate configurations, giving field commanders significant tactical flexibility while maintaining the assault-weight presence that made the original Templar an effective formation anchor.

The most significant change from the original Templar is the Templar III's adoption of a GM 340 Light engine in place of the KalTek 340 Extralight. This substantially improves survivability by eliminating the vulnerability to side torso destruction that plagued the original design, though it comes at the cost of reduced pod space, dropping from forty tons to twenty-nine. The Kallon Type XX Endo Steel chassis and StarGuard CIV armor maintain the same level of protection as the predecessor, and a Heavy-Duty Gyro improves stability under fire.

The primary configuration draws comparison to the proven WHM-8D Warhammer loadout, mounting twin ER PPCs as its primary armament alongside extended-range medium and small lasers. A four-tube short-range missile launcher provides supplementary close-range firepower, with CASE protecting the ammunition. A targeting computer links all energy weapons for improved accuracy, while four additional double heat sinks manage the considerable thermal output of the energy-heavy weapons suite.

While the reduced pod capacity limits the Templar III's ability to mount the heaviest weapon loadouts, the improved chassis durability ensures it can remain in the fight longer. Several configurations take advantage of advanced and Clan-specification technologies to maximize firepower within the tighter weight budget, making the Templar III a more resilient, if somewhat less versatile, successor to the original.

The Templar III's development grew directly from the ashes of the Jihad. With the Kallon Industries factory on Talon destroyed by the Word of Blake, the Federated Suns lost its only production source for the original Templar. General Motors on New Valencia, already producing the Pendragon, a limited-production design loosely based on the Templar chassis, leveraged their familiarity with the platform to develop a modernized successor. Production of the Templar III began around 3100, establishing New Valencia as the new center of Templar-lineage manufacturing.

The Templar III quickly became a popular command 'Mech for AFFS company and battalion commanders, appearing regularly in assault lances throughout Federated Suns frontline formations. During the Capellan invasion campaigns of the Dark Age, lances of Templar IIIs proved effective in combined arms operations. In one notable engagement on Spica in late 3144, a lance of three Templar IIIs and a Salamander inflicted significant casualties on a Capellan 'Mech company, using ER PPCs and targeting computers to devastating effect while channeling the enemy through minefields and narrow streets.

The Templar III's influence extended beyond the Federated Suns. When General Motors resumed Victor production in the 3080s, they redesigned that venerable assault 'Mech to share many components with the Templar III, creating manufacturing efficiencies on New Valencia. Additionally, the custom configuration piloted by the First Prince demonstrated the platform's ability to accept Clan-specification weaponry, producing a significantly more lethal variant that served through the critical campaigns of the late 3140s and into the ilClan era.

The Templar was the first unique Federated Suns OmniMech, an eighty-five ton assault design produced by Kallon Industries and introduced in 3062. Commissioned to address the Federated Suns' lack of an indigenous OmniMech design, the Templar was intended to replace aging designs like the Awesome and Victor in frontline units.

Built around proven off-the-shelf components to reduce costs and speed development, the design offered a generous forty tons of pod space for mission-specific configurations, establishing itself as a powerful and versatile command platform for AFFS assault formations. Though production was eventually disrupted, the Templar proved durable enough to remain in active service well beyond its original production run.

The Templar is built on a lightweight Kallon Type XIX Endo Steel chassis and powered by a KalTek 340 Extralight engine, achieving a respectable top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour for its weight class. Sixteen and a half tons of Starshield A armor provide excellent protection, while CASE in the right torso mitigates ammunition explosion risks. Thirteen fixed double heat sinks manage the baseline thermal load, leaving the full forty tons of pod space available for weapons and equipment.

The primary configuration emphasizes multi-range engagement capability. A Gauss rifle provides devastating long-range firepower, while a large pulse laser, medium pulse laser, and two extended-range medium lasers deliver punishing damage at closer distances. A Streak SRM-4 launcher exploits armor breaches, and an advanced targeting computer links the Gauss rifle and all lasers for enhanced accuracy. This combination makes the Prime an effective battlefield command platform capable of engaging threats at virtually any range.

The Templar's primary vulnerability lies in its reliance on an Extralight engine, which leaves it susceptible to destruction from torso penetration. However, the design philosophy accepted this trade-off to maximize the available pod space, giving field commanders exceptional flexibility in tailoring the 'Mech to specific mission requirements.

The Templar's origins trace directly to the political tensions within the Federated Commonwealth following the Great Refusal in 3060. While both Archon-Prince Victor Steiner-Davion and his sister Archon Katrina dismissed calls for OmniMech development on economic grounds, Field Marshal Duke George Hasek of the Capellan March took matters into his own hands. Hasek directly commissioned Kallon Industries on Talon, a moon of Wernke, to develop the design, backing the project with his own considerable personal fortune. The resulting 'Mech entered production in 3062, just as the FedCom Civil War was erupting.

With House Hasek as the driving force behind its creation, the Templar's initial distribution was heavily weighted toward Capellan March formations. The first units off Kallon's production lines were routed to the Syrtis Fusiliers, with subsequent production runs reaching units such as the Federated Suns Armored Cavalry and the Davion Assault Guards. Throughout the Civil War, Hasek's loyalists ensured these powerful OmniMechs were directed exclusively to units opposing Archon Katrina, particularly excluding Loyalist commands from receiving any. The Twenty-Second Avalon Hussars received several during their defense of Talon, though this alone proved insufficient to secure victory.

The Word of Blake Jihad dealt a catastrophic blow to the Templar program when the Kallon Industries factory on Talon was vaporized, halting all production. The design's intended rise as a flagship AFFS assault 'Mech was set back by decades. General Motors, having obtained access to the Templar's design data through Operation MUSE RED, eventually established production on New Valencia, though they chose to develop a modernized successor rather than restart the original line.

During the Republic era, the Republic Institute of Strategic Combat developed the experimental ORISC configuration, fitting stored Templar chassis with RISC Repeating TSEMP weapons and other volatile experimental technology. The Republic of the Sphere and its wartime Exarch deployed these in false-flag operations under AFFS colors against the Capellan Confederation and Draconis Combine. When Julian Davion visited Terra in 3146, nearly all stored ORISC equipment packages were included in supplies provided to the AFFS, where they saw continued use until every piece of the experimental gear was destroyed through combat, wear, or self-detonation by the end of the 3140s.

Despite the loss of its original production line, surviving Templars remained in AFFS service throughout the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, valued for their durability, flexibility, and the Easy to Maintain quirk that kept aging chassis operational far beyond their expected service life. The Blessed Order's revived First Division also operated a modified configuration, the BLO variant, incorporating improved C3 networking to coordinate their reformed ComStar forces.

General Motors, having obtained access to the Templar's design data through Operation MUSE RED, eventually established production on New Valencia, though they chose to develop a modernized successor rather than restart the original line.

During the Republic era, the Republic Institute of Strategic Combat developed the experimental ORISC configuration, fitting stored Templar chassis with RISC Repeating TSEMP weapons and other volatile experimental technology. The Republic of the Sphere and its wartime Exarch deployed these in false-flag operations under AFFS colors against the Capellan Confederation and Draconis Combine. When Julian Davion visited Terra in 3146, nearly all stored ORISC equipment packages were included in supplies provided to the AFFS, where they saw continued use until every piece of the experimental gear was destroyed through combat, wear, or self-detonation by the end of the 3140s.

Despite the loss of its original production line, surviving Templars remained in AFFS service throughout the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, valued for their durability, flexibility, and the Easy to Maintain quirk that kept aging chassis operational far beyond their expected service life. The Blessed Order's revived First Division also operated a modified configuration, the BLO variant, incorporating improved C3 networking to coordinate their reformed ComStar forces.

The Tenshi, whose name translates to "Angel" in Japanese, is a 95-ton assault OmniMech introduced in 3101 by Luthien Armor Works for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. Designed to be manufactured entirely from Combine-sourced technologies and materials, the Tenshi represented LAW's first foray into OmniMech production for the DCMS. Conceived during a period of covert rearmament following the Jihad, the design answered the Combine's need for a domestically produced assault-weight platform that did not rely on foreign supply chains. A common sight among the Dragon's assault formations, the Tenshi fills the heavy end of the weight spectrum with a flexible platform capable of adapting to multiple battlefield roles through its substantial modular pod system.

The Tenshi was Luthien Armor Works' first OmniMech platform to incorporate several advanced technologies that had entered production in the decades preceding the Jihad. Built on an Endo-Composite internal structure and powered by a Hermes 285 Light fusion engine, the design achieves a remarkable 48 tons of pod capacity, roughly half its total weight. This impressive payload comes at the cost of speed, with a maximum velocity of only 54 kilometers per hour, particularly slower than many comparable assault designs of the era. A Compact Gyro saves additional internal volume, while 18.5 tons of Mitchell Argon Standard armor provides exceptional protection across all locations.

The Tenshi is somewhat labor-intensive to reconfigure due to its complex pod linkage system, making rapid battlefield swaps impractical during time-sensitive operations. This logistical burden is the design's most significant drawback, requiring dedicated technical teams and extended maintenance windows that can strain a formation's operational tempo during fast-moving campaigns.

The Tenshi emerged from Luthien Armor Works as part of a deliberate and covert program to reconstitute the Draconis Combine's shattered military in the aftermath of the Jihad. While publicly adhering to Devlin Stone's disarmament agreements, the Combine quietly pursued new BattleMech projects that would achieve two purposes: manufacture designs using Combine-centric technologies, and rapidly rebuild its decimated 'Mech regiments. Older machines were cycled down to planetary militias to maintain the appearance of compliance while new hardware flowed to frontline units.

The DCMS initially assigned the first Tenshis to the Ghost Regiments, a deliberate choice rooted in both pragmatism and politics. The Ghost Regiments' lower profile within the DCMS meant that should the Tenshi prove a tactical failure, much as the Daboku had nearly a century earlier, the embarrassment would be contained within less prestigious formations. Ghost pilots, however, quickly embraced the new OmniMech and realized its battlefield potential.

In 3103, the Tenshi saw one of its earliest significant engagements when the First Ghost dropped two lances of the assault 'Mechs on the Ghost Bear Dominion world of Grumium. The raiding force struck directly at a weapons stockpile, blasting through a Striker Star before encountering heavier resistance from a Dominion Nova of the First Freemen Cluster. When the Bear commander refused a Trial of Possession, the Ghosts employed massed firepower to devastating effect, cutting down Clan 'Mechs while absorbing heavy return fire. Six of the eight Tenshis survived the engagement and returned to the Combine along with several hundred tons of captured Clan technology, a significant haul that validated the design's combat worthiness.

By the mid-thirty-second century, the Tenshi had become a common sight among the Dragon's frontline 'Mech regiments. At least one full assault company within the Sixteenth Galedon Regulars fielded the type exclusively, demonstrating growing production numbers and the DCMS' deepening confidence in the design. The Tenshi's combination of heavy armor, massive pod capacity, and the flexibility inherent to OmniMech technology ensured its continued prominence within Combine formations as tensions escalated across the Inner Sphere.

text.deployment: Introduced during the Dark Age era, Alternate Configuration AA serves as a modernized evolution of the A configuration's ranged-combat focus. The loadout retains the proven Gauss rifle and SRM-6 combination but replaces the Large Pulse Laser with an ER Large Pulse Laser, extending effective engagement range while maintaining the accuracy advantages of pulse technology. This incremental upgrade reflects the broader trend of Clan manufacturers incorporating improved weapon systems into established configuration frameworks rather than pursuing radical redesigns.

Alternate Configuration B transforms the Summoner into a dedicated missile bombardment platform. Twin LRM-20 launchers provide devastating long-range fire support capability, while a pair of SRM-4 launchers offer close-range defensive firepower. A Narc Missile Beacon allows the Summoner B to designate targets for enhanced missile accuracy from friendly units, and an anti-missile system provides additional protection against return missile fire. This configuration is most effective when operating as part of a coordinated Star, where the Narc beacon multiplies the effectiveness of allied missile platforms.

Alternate Configuration C reconfigures the Summoner as a close-range brawler built around an Ultra Autocannon/20. This devastating weapon provides rapid-fire capability that can shatter opposing armor at short range, supported by a Streak SRM-6 launcher that ensures every missile finds its mark. An ER Large Laser provides some long-range capability during the approach, while an ER Small Laser rounds out the arsenal. The C configuration leverages the Summoner's jump jets aggressively, using mobility to close rapidly and deliver overwhelming close-range firepower before opponents can effectively respond.

Alternate Configuration D emphasizes precision over raw firepower. A pair of ER Large Lasers linked to an advanced Targeting Computer deliver highly accurate fire at extended ranges, supported by two ER Medium Lasers for closer engagements. Twin anti-missile systems provide layered defense against incoming missiles, while a pair of Machine Guns handle anti-infantry duties. Six additional heat sinks manage the thermal load of the all-energy arsenal. The TRO designation of the D as one of the most efficient configurations reflects its ability to sustain accurate fire indefinitely without ammunition concerns.

Alternate Configuration F, introduced during the Jihad era, distributes its firepower symmetrically across both arms. Each arm mounts an Ultra AC/5 and an ER Medium Laser, providing balanced direct-fire capability, while a torso-mounted LRM-10 and additional ER Medium Laser supplement the arsenal. This configuration favors sustained skirmishing engagements, where the rapid-fire autocannons can maintain consistent pressure while the Summoner's mobility allows it to manage range and exposure effectively.

Alternate Configuration G was popularized by warriors of Clan Hell's Horses and centers on an SRM-heavy close-assault philosophy backed by long-range striking power. An ER PPC and ER Large Laser provide the ranged punch to open holes in enemy armor during the approach, while six SRM-4 launchers and a Heavy Small Laser deliver devastating close-range firepower to exploit those breaches. Four additional heat sinks help manage the considerable thermal load, though MechWarriors must still exercise heat discipline when firing the full arsenal. The configuration earned its reputation as a highly aggressive loadout suited to the Horses' combined-arms doctrine.

Alternate Configuration H mirrors the D configuration's precision-fire concept but substitutes Heavy Large Lasers as the primary weapons. These deliver greater damage per shot than standard ER Large Lasers at the cost of reduced range and accuracy at extreme distances, a trade-off offset by the included Targeting Computer. Two ER Medium Lasers provide supplementary fire, an anti-missile system adds defensive capability, and nine additional heat sinks ensure the configuration can sustain its energy-heavy firepower without overheating. The H configuration reflects the Civil War era trend of incorporating heavy laser technology into established Clan designs.

Alternate Configuration HH showcases an array of advanced weapons technology. The centerpiece is a Hyper-Assault Gauss Rifle 20, a rapid-fire kinetic weapon that delivers punishing damage at moderate ranges. A Plasma Cannon provides both direct damage and heat generation against enemy targets, while a Heavy Medium Laser and pair of ER Medium Lasers round out the energy arsenal. An Anti-Personnel Gauss Rifle handles conventional infantry threats. This configuration's diverse weapon mix makes it effective against a wide variety of targets, from heavily armored BattleMechs to infantry formations.

Alternate Configuration J was introduced during the ilClan era and builds its entire combat approach around a massive HAG-40 mounted across the left arm and torso. This Hyper-Assault Gauss Rifle dominates the configuration's weight budget but delivers devastating rapid-fire kinetic barrages capable of shredding armor at medium ranges. Twin Improved Heavy Medium Lasers in the right arm provide close-range backup, while a Light Active Probe in the right torso enhances situational awareness against hidden or electronic warfare-equipped opponents. The J configuration demands aggressive piloting to bring its short-to-medium range arsenal to bear effectively.

Alternate Configuration M closely mirrors the Primary configuration's weapon layout, mounting an ER PPC and LB 10-X Autocannon as its core armament. Where it diverges is in its close-range secondary weapons, replacing the LRM-15 with a Streak SRM-6 launcher and an ER Small Laser. This modification sacrifices indirect fire capability for more reliable close-range damage output, as the Streak system ensures every missile strikes home. The M configuration gained notoriety as a preferred loadout among aggressive Jade Falcon warriors who favored closing to short range to finish engagements decisively.

The Primary configuration exemplifies the Summoner's design philosophy of versatile, all-range combat capability. An ER PPC in the right arm delivers punishing long-range firepower, while an LB 10-X Autocannon in the left arm provides flexible direct fire with the option of cluster or slug ammunition. An LRM-15 launcher in the left torso rounds out the loadout with indirect fire support capability. This balanced combination of energy, ballistic, and missile weapons allows a single Summoner Prime to fill raider, striker, or fire support roles as the situation demands, and it remains the most commonly encountered configuration across all Clans that field the design.

Alternate Configuration Q combines long-range precision with devastating close-range missile salvos. An ER PPC and Large Pulse Laser provide accurate fire at extended ranges, while six SRM-4 launchers deliver an overwhelming barrage at close quarters. A Heavy Medium Laser and Heavy Small Laser add additional close-range punch. This configuration is particularly effective in an ambush role, where the Summoner's jump jets can be used to achieve optimal firing positions before unleashing the full weight of its short-range arsenal against unsuspecting targets.

Alternate Configuration T is a Tiburon Khanate configuration representing a modern refresh of classic Clan Invasion-era design principles. An ER PPC in the right arm provides the primary long-range striking power, supplemented by a ProtoMech AC/8 in the left arm for flexible ballistic firepower at moderate ranges. A Streak LRM-15 in the left torso adds guided missile support with superior accuracy over standard LRM systems. This configuration reflects the ilClan era's emphasis on ammunition efficiency and precision engagement, with the Streak technology ensuring that every missile launched finds its target.

Alternate Configuration Z was developed by the Society, the Clan scientist caste organization that would eventually launch a devastating rebellion against the warrior caste. The configuration incorporates several experimental and Society-exclusive technologies, including a Nova CEWS electronic warfare suite and an experimental ER Large Pulse Laser in the right arm. Eight Anti-Personnel Gauss Rifles in the left arm provide exceptional anti-infantry and anti-battle armor capability, while an improved ATM-12 in the left torso with three tons of ammunition delivers flexible fire support. The Z configuration's reliance on Society-specific technology limited its deployment exclusively to Society forces and their Dark Caste allies during the Wars of Reaving.

text.notes: Dev Note: The various TRO and RS entries from Golden Century don't match in terms of heat sink placement, pod space, etc. I went with the fix that requires no changes to the Record sheets provided, which gives it 11 fixed heat sinks and 24 pod space, rather than a fixed DHS in the LL that doesn't show up on 2 out of 3 configs.

text.deployment: Alternate Configuration A is built for long-range fire support, pairing a Gauss rifle with an ER PPC for powerful direct-fire engagements at extended range. Three LRM-5 launchers provide supplementary indirect fire capability in support of allied units. Two medium pulse lasers offer adequate close-range self-defense against lighter opponents. The Alpha and Prime configurations often deploy together in pairs, with the Alpha providing sustained long-range support while the Prime closes for decisive short-range engagements.

Alternate Configuration D was first deployed in Kuritan and Davion cities, mounting an LB 20-X autocannon supported by two PPCs for effective engagement across multiple range brackets. Uniquely among Sunder configurations, the D variant carries three jump jets, granting mobility uncommon for an assault 'Mech and allowing it to traverse difficult urban terrain. This combination proved extremely deadly when the LB 20-X's cluster rounds could be combined with torso-mounted jump jet mobility to achieve unexpected firing angles.

Alternate Configuration E mounts paired Snub-Nose PPCs and Streak SRM-6 launchers, backed by an ER medium laser and an LB 10-X autocannon. This loadout provides a balanced mix of direct-fire energy weapons and ballistic punch effective from short to medium range. The configuration may represent a factory-built refinement of the mixed-technology R variant developed during Operation Bulldog, achieving a similar combat profile using exclusively Inner Sphere production components.

Introduced during the Dark Age era, Alternate Configuration F incorporates a C3 boosted slave unit for enhanced network coordination. The offensive loadout combines five Clan-built LRM-5 launchers with six Thunderbolt-5 missile launchers, creating a sustained barrage of precision and saturation fire at long range. A single Clan-manufactured ER medium laser provides close-range backup. This configuration reflects the increasing availability of Clan-spec components to Inner Sphere manufacturers during the post-Jihad reconstruction period.

Another Dark Age era addition, Alternate Configuration G stands as a significant escalation in the Sunder's combat capability. A Clan-built ER PPC and Clan LB 20-X autocannon provide tremendous direct-fire punch, supplemented by a Clan ER medium laser. The configuration's most notable feature is a TSEMP cannon, capable of disabling enemy electronics and systems with electromagnetic pulses. A C3 boosted slave unit allows the G variant to share its advanced targeting data across the lance network, making it both a powerful individual combatant and a force multiplier for allied units.

The R configuration is a mixed-technology field upgrade developed in the midst of Operation Bulldog, utilizing captured Clan Smoke Jaguar weapons to bolster SLDF forces during later campaign waves. Twin Clan large pulse lasers provide devastating medium-range firepower, supported by an LB 10-X autocannon. Four ER medium lasers and a pair of Streak SRM-6 launchers round out a weapons array that finally allowed the Sunder to match Clan assault OmniMechs in raw combat effectiveness, a milestone for Inner Sphere OmniMech development.

text.overview: Star Colonel Rikkard Nova Cat pounced on OvKhan Kalasa’s offer to build the iconic Nova Cat Supernova on Angell II. Combining its classic lasers with the endo-steel chassis and heavy armor of late model Supernovas, Delta Aimag still found the space to carry four Coolant Pods by slightly reducing the number of heat sinks. The shocking result was a Supernova that could fire all its weapons without overheating. Unfortunately for Rikkard, Delta Aimag has claimed most of the Supernovas as payment for the factory. Rikkard’s loss is the Inner Sphere’s gain as Clan Sea Fox sells the Supernova far and wide.
text.notableUnits: Captain Bryant Flynn Dunham: The Fourth Regulan Hussars hit Marik in July 3147. Captain “BFD” was happy to see that the defending Clan Protectorate’s Purifier Cluster faced him in direct combat. Implementing his infamous motto of “hey diddle diddle, right up the middle,” his Marauder came face to face with a Protectorate Supernova. Thankfully, the Supernova overheated in the process of dismantling BFD’s ride and was swarmed by Leonidas battle armor. Dunham claimed the fallen ’Mech and pushed on with his unit. At the Winter Palace in Dormuth the Fourth ran into the Shiva Keshik, which scythed through them until BFD made a stand. Utilizing the Supernova’s coolant pods better than its previous pilot, he held the center of the field, acting as a rallying point until the Thirtieth Hussars could come to their aid. Ultimately pushed back after Colonel Mejia’s dishonorable actions, BFD was able to retreat in good order and kept his Supernova when the Hussars were granted hegira in August.

text.deployment: Produced under the auspices of the Clan Protectorate, the Tempest C melds the proven Inner Sphere chassis and armor with a mix of Inner Sphere and Clan-specification weaponry. A Clan-grade large pulse laser and Gauss rifle replace their Inner Sphere counterparts in the arm mounts, while three standard medium lasers are retained. An ATM-9 launcher mounted in the left torso provides tactical flexibility through its variable ammunition types, though only two tons of ammunition somewhat limit this advantage. As with all previous Tempest designs, no CASE has been fitted, a persistent vulnerability that Clan warriors have noted with some disapproval.

production.manufacturer: Irian BattleMechs Unlimited, Irian BattleMechs Unlimited

text.deployment: Regarded as a difficult design to improve upon, it took until the 3130s for Irian BattleMechs Unlimited to produce a formal successor variant. The TMP-4M retains the standard medium lasers and Gauss rifle of the original TMP-3M but replaces the SRM-6 and large pulse laser with five improved jump jets and a snub-nosed PPC. This configuration transforms the Tempest into a more capable skirmisher, with the improved jump jets providing superior mobility while the snub-nosed PPC offers a devastating close-range energy complement to the Gauss rifle's long-range kinetic firepower.

Alternate Configuration A is configured for intermediate to short-range combat, mounting a pair of large pulse lasers and two medium pulse lasers as its primary energy weapons. A pair of seven-tube Multi-Missile Launchers with two tons of ammunition provides flexible fire support across multiple range brackets, allowing the pilot to select optimal ammunition types for the engagement.

Alternate Configuration C mounts a Class 5 Rotary Autocannon as its primary weapon, supported by a pair of extended-range medium lasers, a Streak SRM-6, an ER Small Laser, and a Large Re-Engineered Laser. Three tons of autocannon ammunition and one ton of Streak ammunition provide adequate supply for extended operations, making this a well-rounded configuration effective across multiple engagement ranges.

Alternate Configuration D is specifically designed to counter 'Mechs equipped with reflective armor, mounting four medium re-engineered lasers alongside a Clan-specification LB-10X Autocannon and Clan ER PPC. The combination of kinetic and re-engineered laser weapons ensures effective damage delivery regardless of the target's armor type, with three tons of autocannon ammunition stored in the CASE-protected right torso.

Alternate Configuration A prioritizes long-range engagement with an ER PPC and Ultra Autocannon/10, both linked to a targeting computer for increased accuracy. A Streak SRM-6 provides close-range defense, while a Guardian ECM Suite protects against electronic warfare. Four jump jets grant a hundred-and-twenty meter jump capability, and an additional double heat sink helps manage the considerable thermal load, making this configuration effective at controlling engagement distances.

Alternate Configuration B serves as a sustained fire support platform, pairing an ER PPC with three Rotary Autocannon/2s capable of maintaining withering volumes of fire. Two extended-range medium lasers supplement the arsenal at closer ranges, while four additional double heat sinks ensure the 'Mech can maintain its rate of fire without overheating during prolonged engagements.

Alternate Configuration C is configured for devastating close-range combat, centering its firepower around an LB 20-X Autocannon capable of firing both solid and cluster ammunition. Five medium pulse lasers and an extended-range medium laser provide overwhelming short-range firepower, while a single ER PPC offers long-range defense. Four jump jets provide tactical mobility, allowing the 'Mech to close with opponents or exploit terrain.

Alternate Configuration D emphasizes sustained long-range direct fire, mounting a pair of Light Gauss Rifles in the torso locations and a Large X-Pulse Laser in each arm. This loadout provides consistent damage output at extended ranges without the ammunition dependency of heavier autocannon configurations, though it sacrifices short-range punch compared to other variants.

Alternate Configuration E is purpose-built for command operations, mounting a C3 master computer to coordinate lance-level fire. A Guardian ECM Suite provides electronic protection for the formation, while offensive armament includes a pair of Artemis IV-enhanced LRM-15 launchers, an ER PPC, two medium pulse lasers, and a small laser. This configuration prioritizes the Templar's role as a formation command platform over individual combat power.

Alternate Configuration F serves as another command-oriented variant, carrying a C3 master computer alongside a Heavy PPC and Light Gauss Rifle for significant long-range firepower. Three medium pulse lasers handle closer engagements, and four jump jets provide the mobility needed to maintain optimal positioning for directing lance operations and coordinating formation fire.

Alternate Configuration G appears designed for long-range direct fire support or anti-aircraft duties, mounting three LB 2-X autocannons alongside an ER PPC and Light Gauss Rifle. A C3 slave unit enables the sharing of targeting data with lancemates, enhancing the collective accuracy of the formation while the configuration provides sustained suppressive fire at extended ranges.

Alternate Configuration H combines missile and energy firepower with networking capability, carrying an MRM-30 launcher with Apollo Fire Control System in each arm for devastating medium-range salvos. A pair of Light PPCs and an ER Flamer round out the weapons suite, with a targeting computer enhancing energy weapon accuracy. A C3 slave unit provides data-sharing capability, and four jump jets grant the mobility to maintain effective engagement ranges.

Alternate Configuration I focuses on raw firepower and heat management, mounting two Heavy PPCs and a Gauss Rifle as its primary armament. Fifteen double heat sinks provide the cooling capacity necessary to sustain fire from both PPCs simultaneously, while a C3 slave unit integrates the 'Mech into lance-level targeting networks. This configuration trades flexibility for sheer destructive output at range.

Alternate Configuration R stands as a Dark Age era upgrade incorporating Clan-specification weapons, mounting twin Clan ER PPCs and a Clan LB 10-X autocannon for devastating long-range firepower. Five medium re-engineered lasers provide close-range punch that remains effective against reflective armor. This configuration reflects the increasing availability of Clan technology to Inner Sphere powers during the later Dark Age period.

Alternate Configuration A shifts the Tenshi's focus to medium-range combat with devastating energy firepower. Three Large Variable Speed Pulse Lasers, distributed across both arms and the center torso, deliver concentrated damage at varying ranges. An Apollo-guided MRM-30 launcher with CASE II-protected ammunition provides additional striking power and volume of fire. Five extra Double Heat Sinks and a Coolant Pod help manage the substantial thermal output of this energy-heavy loadout, though sustained alpha strikes remain challenging even with the additional cooling capacity.

text.capabilities:
The Tenshi was Luthien Armor Works' first OmniMech platform to incorporate several advanced technologies that had entered production in the decades preceding the Jihad. Built on an Endo-Composite internal structure and powered by a Hermes 285 Light fusion engine, the design achieves a remarkable 48 tons of pod capacity, roughly half its total weight. This impressive payload comes at the cost of speed, with a maximum velocity of only 54 kilometers per hour, especially slower than many comparable assault designs of the era. A Compact Gyro saves additional internal volume, while 18.5 tons of Mitchell Argon Standard armor provides exceptional protection across all locations.

The Tenshi is somewhat labor-intensive to reconfigure due to its complex pod linkage system, making rapid battlefield swaps impractical during time-sensitive operations. This logistical burden is the design's most significant drawback, requiring dedicated technical teams and extended maintenance windows that can strain a formation's operational tempo during fast-moving campaigns.
text.deployment: Alternate Configuration B is built around a pair of TSEMP Cannons, one mounted in each arm, capable of crippling enemy electronics systems and shutting down opposing 'Mechs entirely. A Heavy PPC provides long-range direct-fire punch, while paired Streak SRM-6 launchers and Medium Pulse Lasers fill close-combat roles against targets already staggered by TSEMP strikes. Three Jump Jets grant the B configuration a mobility advantage unusual for an assault 'Mech of this tonnage, allowing it to navigate difficult terrain and achieve firing positions that would otherwise be inaccessible.

The R configuration employs a mix of Inner Sphere and Clan technologies to create a long-range indirect fire support platform. Twin Extended Long-Range Missile 20 launchers backed by six tons of ammunition can saturate targets at extreme distances well beyond the reach of most conventional weapons. Five Clan-manufactured ER Medium Lasers provide accurate backup firepower at closer ranges, giving this variant some protection against units that manage to close the distance. This configuration transforms the Tenshi from a direct-combat assault 'Mech into a bombardment platform best employed behind friendly lines.
